about: The Lord's Prayer, which Jesus taught His disciples (Mt 6:9–13, and in a shorter form at Lk 11:2–4). It addresses God as Father. It asks that His name be hallowed, His kingdom come, and His will be done, and then asks for daily bread, forgiveness, not to be led into temptation, and deliverance from evil.

seg.tr: Our Father, who art in heaven,

fn.w002: Agrees with “Pater” (w001). The plural expresses a common prayer.
fn.w004: After the vocative the relative clause keeps the 2nd person: “who art”, not “who is”.
fn.w006: Plural, while “cælo” (w018) later in the prayer is singular. The received English renders both as singular.

seg.tr: Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

fn.w013: A subjunctive expressing a petition. The same form “fiat” occurs in Mary's reply at the Annunciation (Lk 1:38).

seg.tr: Give us this day our daily bread.
And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

fn.w030: Dative denoting the person whose debts are forgiven.
fn.w035: The subject spelled out for emphasis.
fn.w036: Indicative within the clause introduced by “sicut” (w033).
fn.w037: Dative dependent on “dimíttimus” (w036). Literally, to the debtors. The received English has those who trespass against us.

seg.tr: And lead us not into temptation,

fn.w040: With the subjunctive “indúcas” (w042) it forms a negative petition: “that Thou not…”.
fn.w042: Subjunctive governed by “ne” (w040). The received English combines the two as “lead us not”.
fn.w043: The preposition “in” with the accusative expresses direction: into temptation.

seg.tr: but deliver us from evil. Amen.

fn.w049: This edition parses “malo” as the neuter noun for evil. The Mass embolism takes it up in the neuter plural, “ab ómnibus malis.” The Catechism also explains that the petition ultimately refers to the Evil One (CCC 2851).

nt.w049: The form is the ablative of both words at once. It can be malum, evil as a thing, or malus, the Evil One. Neither the form nor the sentence decides, and the tradition reads it both ways. This edition takes malum and marks the doubt.
